title: Mercury Precession, Galactic Curves, and Pioneer Anomaly in the Model of Dynamic Quantum Vacuum
content: We present a unified model in which Mercury precession, flat galaxy rotation curves, and the Pioneer anomaly are explained by the variable energy density of a dynamic superfluid quantum vacuum (DQV). In DQV, mass displaces vacuum energy. Angular momentum conservation produces a vortex rotation of the vacuum whose velocity falls with distance. Due to superfluid slip, only a small fraction drags matter. A single slip factor calibrated from Mercury's observed precession predicts all planetary precessions within a few percent, a flat galactic rotation of about two hundred kilometres per second without dark matter, and a Pioneer sunward acceleration decreasing with distance.
